verses.original: לְֽ֭תַאֲוָה יְבַקֵּ֣שׁ נִפְרָ֑ד בְּכָל־ תּ֝וּשִׁיָּ֗ה יִתְגַּלָּֽע׃
verses.transliteration: lə·ṯa·’ă·wāh yə·ḇaq·qêš nip̄·rāḏ bə·ḵāl tū·šî·yāh yiṯ·gal·lā‘
verses.literal: He who isolates himself pursues selfish desires he rebels against all sound judgment
verses.literalPt: Quem vive isolado busca o que deseja e incomoda-se com toda a verdadeira sabedoria.

verses.original: לֹֽא־ יַחְפֹּ֣ץ כְּ֭סִיל בִּתְבוּנָ֑ה כִּ֝֗י אִֽם־ בְּהִתְגַּלּ֥וֹת לִבּֽוֹ׃
verses.transliteration: lō- yaḥ·pōṣ kə·sîl biṯ·ḇū·nāh kî ’im- bə·hiṯ·gal·lō·wṯ lib·bōw
verses.literal: A fool does not delight in understanding but only . . . in airing his opinions
verses.literalPt: O tolo não tem prazer no entendimento, mas tão somente em se revelar tal como é.

verses.original: בְּֽבוֹא־ רָ֭שָׁע בָּ֣א גַם־ בּ֑וּז וְֽעִם־ קָל֥וֹן חֶרְפָּֽה׃
verses.transliteration: bə·ḇō·w- rā·šā‘ bā ḡam- būz wə·‘im- qā·lō·wn ḥer·pāh
verses.literal: With a wicked man comes contempt as well . . . and shame is accompanied by disgrace
verses.literalPt: Quando vier o perverso, vem também o desprezo; e, com a ignomínia, vem o opróbrio.

verses.original: מַ֣יִם עֲ֭מֻקִּים דִּבְרֵ֣י פִי־ אִ֑ישׁ נַ֥חַל נֹ֝בֵ֗עַ מְק֣וֹר חָכְמָֽה׃
verses.transliteration: ma·yim ‘ă·muq·qîm diḇ·rê p̄î- ’îš na·ḥal nō·ḇê·a‘ mə·qō·wr ḥāḵ·māh
verses.literal: The words of a man’s mouth are deep waters the fountain of wisdom is a bubbling brook
verses.literalPt: As palavras da boca do homem são como águas profundas, e a fonte da sabedoria é como ribeiro que corre.

verses.original: שְׂאֵ֣ת פְּנֵי־ רָשָׁ֣ע לֹא־ ט֑וֹב לְהַטּ֥וֹת צַ֝דִּ֗יק בַּמִּשְׁפָּֽט׃
verses.transliteration: śə·’êṯ pə·nê- rā·šā‘ lō- ṭō·wḇ lə·haṭ·ṭō·wṯ ṣad·dîq bam·miš·pāṭ
verses.literal: Showing partiality to the wicked is not good nor is depriving the innocent of justice
verses.literalPt: Não é bom guardar respeito à pessoa do perverso, nem oprimir o justo no juízo.

verses.original: שִׂפְתֵ֣י כְ֭סִיל יָבֹ֣אֽוּ בְרִ֑יב וּ֝פִ֗יו לְֽמַהֲלֻמ֥וֹת יִקְרָֽא׃
verses.transliteration: śip̄·ṯê ḵə·sîl yā·ḇō·’ū ḇə·rîḇ ū·p̄îw lə·ma·hă·lu·mō·wṯ yiq·rā
verses.literal: A fool’s lips bring him strife and his mouth invites a beating
verses.literalPt: Os lábios do tolo metem-se em contendas, e a sua boca provoca açoites.

verses.original: פִּֽי־ כְ֭סִיל מְחִתָּה־ ל֑וֹ וּ֝שְׂפָתָ֗יו מוֹקֵ֥שׁ נַפְשֽׁוֹ׃
verses.transliteration: pî- ḵə·sîl mə·ḥit·tāh- lōw ū·śə·p̄ā·ṯāw mō·w·qêš nap̄·šōw
verses.literal: A fool’s mouth is his ruin and his lips are a snare to his soul
verses.literalPt: A boca do tolo é a sua destruição, e os seus lábios são o laço da sua alma.

verses.original: דִּבְרֵ֣י נִ֭רְגָּן כְּמִֽתְלַהֲמִ֑ים וְ֝הֵ֗ם יָרְד֥וּ חַדְרֵי־ בָֽטֶן׃
verses.transliteration: diḇ·rê nir·gān kə·miṯ·la·hă·mîm wə·hêm yā·rə·ḏū ḥaḏ·rê- ḇā·ṭen
verses.literal: The words of a gossip are like choice morsels that go down into the inmost being . . .
verses.literalPt: As palavras do caluniador são como doces bocados, que penetram até o fundo das entranhas.

verses.original: גַּ֭ם מִתְרַפֶּ֣ה בִמְלַאכְתּ֑וֹ אָ֥ח ה֝֗וּא לְבַ֣עַל מַשְׁחִֽית׃
verses.transliteration: gam miṯ·rap·peh ḇim·laḵ·tōw ’āḥ hū lə·ḇa·‘al maš·ḥîṯ
verses.literal: Whoever is slothful in his work is brother . . . to him who destroys
verses.literalPt: Aquele que é remisso na sua obra é irmão do que é destruidor.

verses.original: מִגְדַּל־ עֹ֭ז שֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֑ה בּֽוֹ־ יָר֖וּץ צַדִּ֣יק וְנִשְׂגָּֽב׃
verses.transliteration: miḡ·dal- ‘ōz šêm Yah·weh bōw- yā·rūṣ ṣad·dîq wə·niś·gāḇ
verses.literal: The name of the LORD is a strong tower the righteous run to it and are safe
verses.literalPt: O nome de Jeová é uma torre forte, à qual o justo se acolhe e está seguro.

verses.original: ה֣וֹן עָ֭שִׁיר קִרְיַ֣ת עֻזּ֑וֹ וּכְחוֹמָ֥ה נִ֝שְׂגָּבָ֗ה בְּמַשְׂכִּיתֽוֹ׃
verses.transliteration: hō·wn ‘ā·šîr qir·yaṯ ‘uz·zōw ū·ḵə·ḥō·w·māh niś·gā·ḇāh bə·maś·kî·ṯōw
verses.literal: A rich man’s wealth is his fortified city it is like a high wall in his imagination
verses.literalPt: Os bens do rico são a sua cidade forte e como um muro alto na sua imaginação.

verses.original: לִפְנֵי־ שֶׁ֭בֶר יִגְבַּ֣הּ לֵב־ אִ֑ישׁ וְלִפְנֵ֖י כָב֣וֹד עֲנָוָֽה׃
verses.transliteration: lip̄·nê·še- še·b̲er yiḡ·bah lêḇ- ’îš wə·lip̄·nê ḵā·ḇō·wḏ ‘ă·nā·wāh
verses.literal: Before his downfall a man’s heart is proud but humility comes before honor
verses.literalPt: Antes da ruína, eleva-se o coração do homem, e adiante da honra vai a humildade.

verses.original: מֵשִׁ֣יב דָּ֭בָר בְּטֶ֣רֶם יִשְׁמָ֑ע אִוֶּ֥לֶת הִיא־ ל֝֗וֹ וּכְלִמָּֽה׃
verses.transliteration: mê·šîḇ dā·ḇār bə·ṭe·rem yiš·mā‘ ’iw·we·leṯ hî- lōw ū·ḵə·lim·māh
verses.literal: He who answers a matter before he hears it this is folly and disgrace to him
verses.literalPt: Quem responde antes de ouvir estultícia lhe é e vergonha.

verses.original: רֽוּחַ־ אִ֭ישׁ יְכַלְכֵּ֣ל מַחֲלֵ֑הוּ וְר֥וּחַ נְ֝כֵאָ֗ה מִ֣י יִשָּׂאֶֽנָּה׃
verses.transliteration: rū·aḥ- ’îš yə·ḵal·kêl ma·ḥă·lê·hū wə·rū·aḥ nə·ḵê·’āh mî yiś·śā·’en·nāh
verses.literal: The spirit of a man can endure his sickness but who can survive a broken spirit
verses.literalPt: O espírito do homem o sustentará na enfermidade, mas quem poderá levantar a um espírito quebrantado?

verses.original: לֵ֣ב נָ֭בוֹן יִקְנֶה־ דָּ֑עַת וְאֹ֥זֶן חֲ֝כָמִ֗ים תְּבַקֶּשׁ־ דָּֽעַת׃
verses.transliteration: lêḇ nā·ḇō·wn yiq·neh- dā·‘aṯ wə·’ō·zen ḥă·ḵā·mîm tə·ḇaq·qeš- dā·‘aṯ
verses.literal: The heart of the discerning acquires knowledge and the ear of the wise seeks it out
verses.literalPt: O coração do inteligente adquire conhecimento, e o ouvido dos sábios busca ao conhecimento.

verses.original: מַתָּ֣ן אָ֭דָם יַרְחִ֣יב ל֑וֹ וְלִפְנֵ֖י גְדֹלִ֣ים יַנְחֶֽנּוּ׃
verses.transliteration: mat·tān ’ā·ḏām yar·ḥîḇ lōw wə·lip̄·nê ḡə·ḏō·lîm yan·ḥen·nū
verses.literal: A man’s gift opens doors for him and brings him before great men
verses.literalPt: Os presentes do homem alegram-lhe o caminho e levam-no perante os grandes.

verses.original: צַדִּ֣יק הָרִאשׁ֣וֹן בְּרִיב֑וֹ יָבֹא רֵ֝עֵ֗הוּ וַחֲקָרֽוֹ׃
verses.transliteration: ṣad·dîq hā·ri·šō·wn bə·rî·ḇōw yå̄·ḇō wa·ḥă·qā·rōw
verses.literal: The first to state his case seems right until another comes and cross-examines him
verses.literalPt: O primeiro que pleiteia a sua causa parece justo, mas vem a outra parte e o sonda.

verses.original: מִ֭דְיָנִים יַשְׁבִּ֣ית הַגּוֹרָ֑ל וּבֵ֖ין עֲצוּמִ֣ים יַפְרִֽיד׃
verses.transliteration: miḏ·yā·nîm yaš·bîṯ hag·gō·w·rāl ū·ḇên ‘ă·ṣū·mîm yap̄·rîḏ
verses.literal: Casting the lot . . . ends quarrels and separates strong opponents
verses.literalPt: A sorte faz cessar os pleitos e decide entre os poderosos.

verses.original: אָ֗ח נִפְשָׁ֥ע מִקִּרְיַת־ עֹ֑ז וּמְדוֹנִים כִּבְרִ֥יחַ אַרְמֽוֹן׃
verses.transliteration: ’āḥ nip̄·šā‘ miq·qir·yaṯ- ‘ōz ū·mə·ḏō·nīm kiḇ·rî·aḥ ’ar·mō·wn
verses.literal: An offended brother is harder to win than a fortified city and disputes are like the bars of a castle
verses.literalPt: O irmão ofendido é mais difícil de conquistar do que uma cidade forte, e tais contendas são como os ferrolhos dum castelo.

verses.original: מִפְּרִ֣י פִי־ אִ֭ישׁ תִּשְׂבַּ֣ע בִּטְנ֑וֹ תְּבוּאַ֖ת שְׂפָתָ֣יו יִשְׂבָּֽע׃
verses.transliteration: mip·pə·rî p̄î- ’îš tiś·ba‘ biṭ·nōw tə·ḇū·’aṯ śə·p̄ā·ṯāw yiś·bā‘
verses.literal: From the fruit of his mouth a man’s belly is filled with the harvest from his lips he is satisfied
verses.literalPt: O ventre dum homem se fartará do fruto da sua boca, e com os renovos dos seus lábios, estará satisfeito.

verses.original: מָ֣וֶת וְ֭חַיִּים בְּיַד־ לָשׁ֑וֹן וְ֝אֹהֲבֶ֗יהָ יֹאכַ֥ל פִּרְיָֽהּ׃
verses.transliteration: mā·weṯ wə·ḥay·yîm bə·yaḏ- lā·šō·wn wə·’ō·hă·ḇe·hā yō·ḵal pir·yāh
verses.literal: Life and death are in the power of the tongue and those who love it will eat its fruit
verses.literalPt: A morte e a vida estão no poder da língua, cujos amadores comerão dos frutos dela.

verses.original: מָצָ֣א אִ֭שָּׁה מָ֣צָא ט֑וֹב וַיָּ֥פֶק רָ֝צ֗וֹן מֵיְהוָֽה׃
verses.transliteration: mā·ṣā ’iš·šāh mā·ṣā ṭō·wḇ way·yā·p̄eq rā·ṣō·wn Yah·weh
verses.literal: He who finds a wife finds a good thing and obtains favor from the LORD
verses.literalPt: Quem acha uma esposa acha o bem e alcança o favor de Jeová.

verses.original: תַּחֲנוּנִ֥ים יְדַבֶּר־ רָ֑שׁ וְ֝עָשִׁ֗יר יַעֲנֶ֥ה עַזּֽוֹת׃
verses.transliteration: ta·ḥă·nū·nîm yə·ḏab·ber- rāš wə·‘ā·šîr ya·‘ă·neh ‘az·zō·wṯ
verses.literal: The poor man pleads for mercy . . . but the rich man answers harshly
verses.literalPt: O pobre fala com súplicas, mas o rico responde com asperezas.

verses.original: אִ֣ישׁ רֵ֭עִים לְהִתְרֹעֵ֑עַ וְיֵ֥שׁ אֹ֝הֵ֗ב דָּבֵ֥ק מֵאָֽח׃
verses.transliteration: ’îš rê·‘îm lə·hiṯ·rō·‘ê·a‘ wə·yêš ’ō·hêḇ dā·ḇêq mê·’āḥ
verses.literal: A man of many companions may come to ruin but there is a friend who stays closer than a brother
verses.literalPt: Quem faz para si muitos amigos fá-los para sua desgraça; mas há um amigo que é mais chegado do que um irmão.
